input_signals.name: Unabsorbed External Financing
input_signals.expression: WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(ADD(SUB(sstk, prstkc), SUB(dltis, dltr)), at), RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), at)), 1)
input_signals.hypothesis: External financing that exceeds disclosed intangible investment predicts lower subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: Both components are flow-to-assets measures, so their difference estimates financing not plausibly absorbed by R&D or advertising rather than multiplying two standalone anomaly ranks. High values identify potentially market-timed financing, while low values identify organic or intangible-intensive investment with little external issuance.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( sub( ratio( add( sub( sstk, prstkc ), sub( dltis, dltr ) ), at ), ratio( add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ), at ) ), 1 )

input_signals.name: Issuance Commercialization Gap
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(sstk, prstkc), at), 1)), WINSOR(SUB(DELTA(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), at), 1), DELTA(RATIO(sale, at), 1)), 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: Net equity issuance predicts lower returns when intangible intensity is rising faster than sales productivity.
input_signals.reasoning: A widening gap between intangible investment intensity and sales-to-assets indicates that newly financed spending has not yet produced commercial traction, making an innovation-based issuance narrative more vulnerable to overvaluation. The continuous gap avoids a zero-heavy gate, while the issuance rank emphasizes high issuers without reversing the signal for repurchasers.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( winsor( ratio( sub( sstk, prstkc ), at ), 1 ) ), winsor( sub( delta( ratio( add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ), at ), 1 ), delta( ratio( sale, at ), 1 ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Research Duration Mismatch
input_signals.expression: MUL(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(dlc, at), RATIO(dltt, at)), 1), WINSOR(MA(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 3), 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: Short-term rather than long-term debt exposure predicts lower returns among firms maintaining substantial R&D programs.
input_signals.reasoning: Research projects have long and uncertain payoff horizons, making current-debt dependence a source of rollover pressure and premature project termination. The signed maturity spread replaces the prior zero-inflated gross-debt construction and tests financing suitability rather than assuming all creditor funding is favorable.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( sub( ratio( dlc, at ), ratio( dltt, at ) ), 1 ), winsor( ma( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), sale ), 3 ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Intangible-Rent Deleveraging
input_signals.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(dltr, dltis), at), 1), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(sale, cogs), ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0))), sale), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Net debt retirement predicts higher returns when the firm generates strong operating surplus after intangible expenditures.
input_signals.reasoning: Productive intangible financing should eventually generate rents that permit deleveraging, whereas continued borrowing without such rents suggests financing dependence. The signed debt-retirement term determines direction, while the continuous rent rank scales conviction without an indicator-driven zero mass or another variation of the net-financing gap.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( ratio( sub( dltr, dltis ), at ), 1 ), rank( winsor( ratio( sub( sub( sale, cogs ), add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ) ), sale ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Lagged-Asset Rent Deleveraging
input_signals.expression: MUL(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), LAG(at, 1))), 1), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(sale, cogs), ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0))), sale), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Debt reductions scaled by beginning assets predict higher returns when supported by strong operating surplus after intangible expenditures.
input_signals.reasoning: Deflating the change in debt by lagged assets measures actual deleveraging without mechanically rewarding contemporaneous asset growth. The intangible-rent rank then emphasizes debt reduction supported by productive innovation rather than distressed contraction or refinancing activity.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( neg( ratio( delta( add( dltt, dlc ), 1 ), lag( at, 1 ) ) ), 1 ), rank( winsor( ratio( sub( sub( sale, cogs ), add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ) ), sale ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Joint Rent-Deleveraging Quality
input_signals.expression: MIN(RANK(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), LAG(at, 1))), 1)), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(sale, cogs), ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0))), sale), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms jointly exhibiting verified debt reduction and strong intangible-adjusted operating rents earn higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: Debt reduction generated a strong Fama-MacBeth relation but negligible portfolio alpha when rents merely scaled a signed deleveraging measure. The minimum-rank conjunction creates a high signal only when both deleveraging and intangible-rent quality are strong, producing a more economically homogeneous long portfolio without imposing sparse indicators.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( rank( winsor( neg( ratio( delta( add( dltt, dlc ), 1 ), lag( at, 1 ) ) ), 1 ) ), rank( winsor( ratio( sub( sub( sale, cogs ), add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ) ), sale ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Identifiable-Intangible Term Match
input_signals.expression: MUL(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(dltt, at), RATIO(dlc, at)), 1), WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(COALESCE(intan, 0), COALESCE(gdwl, 0)), at), 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: Long-term rather than short-term debt financing predicts higher returns when backed by identifiable intangible assets net of goodwill.
input_signals.reasoning: Identifiable intangible assets are longer-lived and relatively more contractible than expensed research or residual acquisition goodwill, making long-term debt the better maturity match. This tests financing-term suitability for recognized intangible capital rather than another goodwill-growth or external-issuance anomaly.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( sub( ratio( dltt, at ), ratio( dlc, at ) ), 1 ), winsor( ratio( sub( coalesce( intan, 0 ), coalesce( gdwl, 0 ) ), at ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Dual-Validated Intangible Deleveraging
input_signals.expression: MIN(RANK(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), LAG(at, 1))), 1)), RANK(SUMRANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(sale, cogs), ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0))), sale), 1), WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), 1), LAG(at, 1)), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Deleveraging predicts higher returns when supported jointly by strong intangible-adjusted rents and continued intangible reinvestment.
input_signals.reasoning: Rent quality previously supplied the stronger Fama-MacBeth slope, while reinvestment validation supplied the stronger portfolio alpha. Combining both productive-use channels before applying the deleveraging conjunction seeks firms that can reduce debt without harvesting or abandoning their intangible capital base.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( rank( winsor( neg( ratio( delta( add( dltt, dlc ), 1 ), lag( at, 1 ) ) ), 1 ) ), rank( sumrank( winsor( ratio( sub( sub( sale, cogs ), add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ) ), sale ), 1 ), winsor( ratio( delta( add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ), 1 ), lag( at, 1 ) ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Unabsorbed Rollover Financing
input_signals.expression: MIN(RANK(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(ADD(SUB(sstk, prstkc), SUB(dltis, dltr)), at), RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), at)), 1)), RANK(WINSOR(MUL(SUB(RATIO(dlc, at), RATIO(dltt, at)), MA(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 3)), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms jointly exhibiting unabsorbed external financing and a short-maturity mismatch with R&D investment earn lower subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: Unabsorbed financing and research-duration mismatch are the two archived mechanisms with the clearest alignment between Fama-MacBeth and FF5 portfolio evidence. Their conjunction targets firms whose financing is both weakly tied to intangible deployment and fragile in maturity, rather than merely adding two standalone anomaly scores.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( rank( winsor( sub( ratio( add( sub( sstk, prstkc ), sub( dltis, dltr ) ), at ), ratio( add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ), at ) ), 1 ) ), rank( winsor( mul( sub( ratio( dlc, at ), ratio( dltt, at ) ), ma( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), sale ), 3 ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Research-Uncertainty Maturity Support
input_signals.expression: MUL(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(dltt, at), RATIO(dlc, at)), 1), WINSOR(VOL(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 3), 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: Long-term rather than short-term debt exposure predicts higher returns when R&D intensity is uncertain.
input_signals.reasoning: Volatile research programs require financing that can absorb uncertain timing and avoid near-term rollover pressure, making maturity support more important than for stable programs. This replaces the mismatched level-plus-change augmentation with a distinct uncertainty mechanism and uses a signed maturity spread to avoid the clumpy portfolios generated by the prior total-debt-times-volatility signal.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( sub( ratio( dltt, at ), ratio( dlc, at ) ), 1 ), winsor( vol( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), sale ), 3 ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Rent-Backed Sustained Debt Retirement
input_signals.expression: MIN(RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(TS_SUM(SUB(dltr, dltis), 3), at), 1)), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(sale, cogs), ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0))), sale), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Sustained net debt retirement predicts higher returns when supported by strong operating rents after intangible expenditures.
input_signals.reasoning: Cumulative debt retirement conditioned only on R&D intensity produced strongly adverse portfolio alpha, suggesting that some firms were deleveraging under funding pressure rather than graduating from external finance. Requiring high intangible-adjusted rents separates voluntary, internally funded repayment from forced deleveraging while preserving the multi-period flow measure.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( rank( winsor( ratio( ts_sum( sub( dltr, dltis ), 3 ), at ), 1 ) ), rank( winsor( ratio( sub( sub( sale, cogs ), add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ) ), sale ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Unabsorbed Research-Shock Financing
input_signals.expression: MIN(RANK(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(ADD(SUB(sstk, prstkc), SUB(dltis, dltr)), at), RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), at)), 1)), RANK(WINSOR(MUL(SUB(RATIO(dltis, at), RATIO(sstk, at)), SUB(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), MA(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 3))), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms jointly exhibiting unabsorbed external financing and a financing-source mismatch with an R&D shock earn lower subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The unabsorbed-financing leg supplies strong monotonic and portfolio evidence, while research-shock mismatch contributes a distinct source-timing channel with strong negative portfolio alpha. Their conjunction targets external financing that is both weakly connected to intangible deployment and poorly matched to the direction of current research needs.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( rank( winsor( sub( ratio( add( sub( sstk, prstkc ), sub( dltis, dltr ) ), at ), ratio( add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ), at ) ), 1 ) ), rank( winsor( mul( sub( ratio( dltis, at ), ratio( sstk, at ) ), sub( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), sale ), ma( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), sale ), 3 ) ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Debt-Share Research Uncertainty Support
input_signals.expression: MUL(COALESCE(RATIO(SUB(dltt, dlc), ADD(dltt, dlc)), 0), WINSOR(VOL(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 3), 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: A greater long-term share of debt predicts higher returns for firms with uncertain R&D intensity.
input_signals.reasoning: Dividing the maturity balance by total debt removes leverage magnitude and isolates whether existing debt is predominantly long- or short-term. Debt-free firms have no maturity support and receive a neutral zero, while the signed share supplies both long- and short-maturity portfolio tails without the non-negative clumping of the earlier rollover-share construction.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( coalesce( ratio( sub( dltt, dlc ), add( dltt, dlc ) ), 0 ), winsor( vol( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), sale ), 3 ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Rent-Scarce Research Rollover
input_signals.expression: MUL(WINSOR(MUL(SUB(RATIO(dlc, at), RATIO(dltt, at)), MA(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 3)), 1), RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(sale, cogs), ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0))), sale), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Short-maturity financing of sustained R&D predicts especially low returns when post-intangible operating rents are weak.
input_signals.reasoning: Firms with limited current rents have less internal capacity to refinance short-term claims without disrupting long-horizon research, making the duration mismatch more severe. The continuous low-rent rank preserves the successful signed maturity tails while targeting the firms most exposed to rollover-induced underinvestment.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( mul( sub( ratio( dlc, at ), ratio( dltt, at ) ), ma( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), sale ), 3 ) ), 1 ), rank( neg( winsor( ratio( sub( sub( sale, cogs ), add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ) ), sale ), 1 ) ) ) )
